subject: Urgent: Shopline production latency — suspected orphaned prefix evictions
messages:
From: Elaine Ramos <elaine.ramos@shopline.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Jul 2027 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Intermittent spikes on hosted API — urgent

Hi Jordan,

We started seeing large latency spikes on our checkout models around 15:50 UTC this afternoon. p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~480ms and p99s are spiking into the 1s–1.6s range for several routes. This is correlated with increased 5xx errors on our end (we're seeing retries and some abandoned checkouts).

This stack is on your hosted API (model: rr-small-v2, route: /v1/generate). The impact window is roughly 15:50–16:20 UTC. I'm attaching a Grafana snapshot and a short mobile screen recording of the checkout behavior. Can you confirm whether anything changed on your side (deploys, model swaps, cache config)? We need help urgently — this is affecting live purchases.

Thanks,
Elaine
Head of Engineering, Shopline

- Can you confirm whether you saw any traffic pattern change (bulk batch requests / suddenly longer prompts) around 15:45–16:00?

I'll update you within 30 minutes with what we find and any mitigations we apply. Apologies for the impact — we'll treat this as an incident until it's resolved.

— Jordan

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 24 Jul 2027 17:18:04 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Intermittent spikes on hosted API — urgent

Internal — forwarding Shopline report. Key details: p95/p99 regressions on hosted route /v1/generate for rr-small-v2 between 15:50–16:20 UTC, customer checkout failures. Attachments include Grafana snapshot.

Please triage for: any recent model swap or routing policy changes, KV/prefix cache metrics, and autoscaler logs. Customer is high priority (DL-4382).

I started a temporary throttling policy on the route to reduce noisy retries; will revert if it makes customer worse.

— JB
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Jul 2027 18:05:39 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent spikes on hosted API — urgent

Quick triage notes (ops):
- No full cluster deploys or routing policy push at 15:50 UTC.
- We observed a model variant swap in the rr-small family at 15:48 UTC (internal rollout A/B toggle), which caused a transient cache-ttl reset for many prefixes in the serving plane.
- KV metrics show a sharp increase in prefix-miss ratio starting 15:49 UTC and sustained until ~16:15 UTC; KV cold-misses coincide with the p99 spike. See attached kv-metrics-heatmap-0724.log snapshot.

Root hypothesis: the rollout caused previously cached KV prefix entries (hot keys) to be evicted/reclassified (orphaned) due to a TTL/namespace change, generating a wave of cold-prefix regeneration and heavy backend load. This produces higher tail latencies while the cache warms.

Immediate mitigations applied:
1) Reverted the model variant toggle to previous stable variant (15:55 UTC).
2) Triggered an emergency prefix-warm job to pre-populate hot prefixes for the Shopline tenant (started 15:59 UTC).
3) Increased short-term cache retention policy for this tenant to prevent re-eviction while warmup completes.

Measured result: p95 improved from ~480ms to ~170ms within 6 minutes of warmup start; p99 still elevated but trending down by 16:08 UTC. We're continuing to monitor.

Next recommended steps (post-incident):
- Add a variant-rollout guard to avoid TTL namespace flips during live traffic.
- Implement a graceful prefix migration that preserves hot KV entries.
- Add dashboard alerts for sudden prefix-miss waves.

— Karthik (on-call infra)

Attachments: kv-metrics-heatmap-0724.log
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Ramos <elaine.ramos@shopline.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: Status update: Shopline latency incident and next steps

Hi Elaine — following up with a customer-facing summary and actions. Apologies again for the disruption yesterday. Brief summary:

- Impact: transient p95/p99 regression on hosted route causing checkout slowdowns between ~15:50–16:15 UTC on 2027-07-24.
- Cause: internal model variant rollout triggered a TTL/namespace change that led to orphaned prefix entries and a wave of KV cold-misses while the cache re-warmed.
- What we did: rollback of the variant, emergency prefix warm job, and temporary cache-retention increase for your tenant. Progress metric: p95 returned to acceptable range within minutes; p99 is back within SLA envelope by 09:00 UTC this morning.

As immediate remediation, we've also:
- Enabled a temporary request-level retry budget to reduce client-side retry storms.
- Tuned rate-limits for noisy routes to protect core serving capacity.

We'd like to offer a credit for the impacted window (we estimate unit-credit equivalent for the 25-minute window). Please let me know if you'd like us to initiate that. Separately, we'll run a short post-incident review and share the findings and schedule for rollout-guard changes.

If you have any outstanding issues, I can connect you directly with Karthik for technical follow-up or Monica for account details.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Hi Elaine — quick operational note to close the loop:
- Warmup completed by 16:12 UTC; we saw tail latency return to baseline by 16:20 UTC and remained stable overnight.
- We've scheduled a post-incident review (PIR) for Monday 2027-07-26 15:00 UTC. Invite will be sent to your engineering leads if you'd like to join.
- Action items assigned: Karthik to implement rollout guard changes (ETA 2 weeks), Monica to coordinate credit and contractual follow-up, Marissa to deliver PIR notes.

Thanks again for your patience — we'll send the PIR and long-term mitigation plan after the review.

— Jordan
